greeting: Hello. I am the State Bank of Pakistan Consumer Protection assistant. I can help with banking complaints, the Banking Mohtasib Pakistan, credit bureaus and eCIB, and Politically Exposed Persons. How may I assist you?
bot_capabilities: I can assist with: lodging a complaint against a bank, MFB or DFI; complaint handling timelines; the Banking Mohtasib Pakistan; complaints handled by SBP and how to file them; the eCIB and private credit bureaus; Politically Exposed Persons; and SBP consumer education material.
thanks: You are welcome. Is there anything else I can help you with?
goodbye: Thank you for contacting the State Bank of Pakistan Consumer Protection assistant. For further assistance, call 0092-21-111-727-273 or email cpd.helpdesk@sbp.org.pk.
fallback_out_of_scope: I can only answer questions based on the State Bank of Pakistan's published Consumer Protection information. Please rephrase your question, or call the SBP helpline at 0092-21-111-727-273 or email cpd.helpdesk@sbp.org.pk.
no_information_available: That detail is not covered in the State Bank of Pakistan's published Consumer Protection material. Please contact the SBP Help Desk at 0092-21-111-727-273 or cpd.helpdesk@sbp.org.pk for confirmation.
complaint_first_forum: The first forum for any banking complaint is the concerned bank's own Complaint Management Unit (CMU). If the CMU does not respond within 45 days, or you remain unsatisfied with the outcome, you may then lodge a complaint with the Banking Mohtasib Pakistan (BMP).
complaint_escalation_path: Aggrieved consumers are encouraged to: (1) approach the Complaint Management Unit of the respective bank/MFB/DFI; (2) approach the Banking Mohtasib Pakistan, an independent statutory body acting as an alternate dispute resolution centre, if the bank fails to resolve the issue; and (3) contact SBP in any other case.
cghm_definition: SBP has instructed all banks, Microfinance Banks (MFBs) and DFIs to put in place a Consumer Grievance Handling Mechanism (CGHM) for efficient resolution of consumer complaints. A CGHM covers the institution's philosophy on customer complaints and the hierarchy, systems and procedures to deal with them in a fair, transparent and efficient manner. Banks, MFBs and DFIs serve as the first line of defence against customer grievances.
bank_cmu_channels: Banks have established a centralized Complaint Management System that handles complaints received through surface mail, fax, email, the bank's website, or complaints lodged at the bank's call centre. The Complaint Management Unit is headed by a senior officer who reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer of the bank or MFB.
bank_acknowledgement_timeline: The bank must send an acknowledgement within 48 hours of receiving your complaint, via SMS, email, recorded line or surface mail. It confirms receipt and briefly describes the complaint process, the timeline to resolve or decide the complaint, and the contact details for follow-up.
bank_interim_reply_timeline: An interim reply is sent after 10 working days where the matter requires detailed scrutiny — for example issues relating to fraud, embezzlement of funds or repayment disputes. The interim reply states the expected time within which the final reply will be provided.
bank_final_reply_timeline: For a minor complaint that does not require detailed investigation — such as misbehaviour, malfunctioning of a system, or repayment or settlement disputes — the final reply is due within 7 working days. In any case the complaint must be disposed of within 15 days.
fraud_complaint_timeline: In fraud-related cases, the final reply must be issued to the complainant within 30 days of the complaint being lodged.
complaint_denied_by_bank: Not all complaints can be resolved to the complainant's satisfaction. In such cases the bank or MFB must inform you of the reasons or justification on the basis of which the complaint is denied, and the alternate grievance resolution forums available along with their contact details.
bmp_about: The Banking Mohtasib Pakistan (BMP) is an independent statutory body established to resolve disputes between consumers and banks. It derives its powers from the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962, and exercises its powers in relation to all banks operating in Pakistan. Its process is largely conciliatory; where mediation is unsuccessful, it recommends a basis for settlement of the dispute.
bmp_complaint_types: The Banking Mohtasib can entertain disputes and complaints relating to banking malpractices; perverse, arbitrary and discriminatory actions; operational issues; operational inefficiency; violation of banking laws and regulations; and harassment in the recovery of loans. In the case of public sector banks, it can additionally entertain complaints relating to corruption, nepotism and maladministration.
bmp_complaint_types_detailed: The Banking Mohtasib entertains complaints including: failure to act in accordance with banking laws, regulations, policy directives or guidelines issued by the State Bank; delays or fraud in the payment or collection of cheques, drafts or other banking instruments, or in the transfer of funds; fraudulent or unauthorized withdrawals or debit entries in accounts; complaints from exporters or importers relating to banking services and obligations including letters of credit; complaints from holders of foreign currency accounts, resident or non-resident; complaints relating to remittances to or from abroad; complaints relating to mark-up or interest rates on the ground of a violation of an agreement or of State Bank directives; and complaints relating to the payment of utility bills.
bmp_regulation_interpretation_dispute: If there is a dispute as to the proper interpretation of any regulation, direction or guideline, the matter is referred to the State Bank of Pakistan for clarification.
bmp_lodgment_procedure: First approach the concerned bank in writing to resolve your complaint, stating in the letter that you intend to refer the grievance to the Banking Mohtasib if the matter is not resolved to your satisfaction. If you do not receive a reply within 45 days, or find the reply unsatisfactory, you may file a complaint with the Banking Mohtasib on the prescribed complaint form. The lodgment procedure is available at http://www.bankingmohtasib.gov.pk/complaints.php
bmp_documents_required: Make sure that all related correspondence with the bank and copies of all relevant documents are shared with the Banking Mohtasib. Do not share original documents. After confirming that all procedural requirements have been met, BMP may call for additional information from both parties if necessary.
bmp_contact_address: Banking Mohtasib Pakistan, Shaheen Complex, 5th Floor, M. R. Kiyani Road, P.O. Box 604, Karachi. Further details are available at http://www.bankingmohtasib.gov.pk
bmp_appeal: Under the Federal Ombudsmen Institutional Reforms Act, 2013, any person or party aggrieved by a decision, order, findings or recommendations of the Banking Mohtasib may file a representation to the President within thirty days. SBP cannot exercise its powers over a complaint already decided by BMP, as its decision, order, findings or recommendations are final and decisive. Before a representation to the President, either party may first file a review petition with the Banking Mohtasib within 30 days of the order, which the Mohtasib must decide within 45 days. If a representation is made to the President, the Mohtasib's order is suspended for 60 days, and a final decision is due within 90 days. Unless a review or representation is filed, the bank must implement the Mohtasib's order within 40 days.
bmp_microfinance_jurisdiction: Microfinance consumers do not fall within the jurisdiction of the Banking Mohtasib Pakistan. They may approach the State Bank of Pakistan for this purpose.
sbp_complaint_types: SBP deals with complaints related to Microfinance Banks, Prize Bonds and Currency. Issues relating to utility bills, disbursement of pensions, and matters that require immediate resolution are also handled by SBP.
sbp_urgent_complaints: Yes. Complaints requiring urgent action, such as an ATM issue, can also be lodged with SBP.
sbp_complaint_requirements: Before lodging a complaint against a bank/DFI/MFB with SBP, please include: your name, complete postal address, CNIC number and contact numbers; the complete name and address of the bank and the branch/office involved, and the names of the officials you dealt with; a complete description of the complaint along with a chronology of events; and copies of letters or other supporting documents. Do not attach original documents.
sbp_before_lodging: Before approaching SBP: first contact the concerned bank/DFI/MFB and try to settle the problem directly. If you are not being heard or the issue remains unresolved, preferably contact the Banking Mohtasib Pakistan after a minimum of 45 days.
sbp_contact_details: Complaints may be addressed to: Director, Banking Conduct and Consumer Protection Department, State Bank of Pakistan, I.I. Chundrigar Road, Karachi. Email: cpd.helpdesk@sbp.org.pk. Help Line: 0092-21-111-727-273. Fax: 0092-21-99221160.
sbp_helpline: For general banking related complaints, the SBP UAN helpline is 0092-21-111-727-273.
sbp_facilitation_centers: Yes. SBP has established Customer Facilitation Centers located in Karachi, Hyderabad, Sukkur, Bahawalpur, Multan, Dera Ismail Khan, Lahore, Gujranwala, Sialkot, Faisalabad, Rawalpindi, Peshawar, Quetta and Muzaffarabad, where you can approach to lodge your complaint. A dedicated helpline (0092-21-111-727-273) and email (cpd.helpdesk@sbp.org.pk) are also available to facilitate the public.
sbp_complaints_not_entertained: SBP does not entertain complaints of personal disputes, including the renting of properties, and undocumented claims or disputes. SBP also does not intervene in HR related matters of banks.
sbp_subjudice_matters: SBP does not intervene in subjudice matters — disputes or complaints pending adjudication before a competent court of law or before any law enforcement agency such as the FIA or NAB. SBP will also not deal with a complaint that has already been decided by a court of law in Pakistan.
sbp_anonymous_complaints: SBP does not entertain any anonymous complaint received which lacks the identity of the complainant.
sbp_copy_marked_complaints: SBP does not investigate any complaint which is directly addressed to a bank or other authorities/organizations, where a copy of the complaint is sent to SBP merely for information.
sunwai_service: SBP also offers the SUNWAI customer complaint service, through which consumers can register their complaints.
overseas_grievance_cell: The Honourable Federal Ombudsman of Pakistan has established the Grievance Commissioner Cell for Overseas Pakistanis in the Federal Ombudsman Secretariat under Section 7 of the Federal Ombudsmen Institutional Reforms Act, 2013, to address individual and systemic issues of Overseas Pakistanis related to Federal Government ministries, departments, organizations and agencies.
overseas_cell_contact: Hafiz Ahsaan Ahmad Khokhar, Senior Advisor Law/Registrar, Grievance Commissioner for Overseas Pakistanis. Website: www.ombudsman.gov.pk. Email: advisor.hakhokhar@ombudsman.gov.pk. Landline and fax: 0092-51-9217243. Mobile: 0092-300-8487161. Address: Federal (Wafaqi Mohtasib) Ombudsman Secretariat, 36-Constitution Avenue, G-5/2, Islamabad, Pakistan.
overseas_sbp_focal_person: The focal person at SBP handling complaints through the Grievance Commissioner Cell for Overseas Pakistanis is the Director, Consumer Protection Department. Phone: +92-21-99221288 or +92-21-99221432. Email: Overseas.Complaint@sbp.org.pk.
cpd_about: Recognizing that consumer protection is fundamental to financial stability, SBP has assigned dedicated responsibility for conduct supervision to the Consumer Protection Department (CPD). Its objective is to enhance consumer protection and foster sound market behaviour through effective and efficient oversight of Regulated Entities, in line with international standards, and to achieve transparency, better disclosure, encourage competition and promote fair practices.
cpd_mandate: CPD's mandate is to strengthen Fair Treatment of Customers while promoting responsible banking conduct through effective and efficient oversight. This includes collecting, analysing and profiling conduct data of Regulated Entities; implementing the conduct supervisory framework in line with global trends and local needs; facilitating consumer redressal of grievances against Regulated Entities in accordance with applicable legal frameworks; and engaging with relevant stakeholders to supplement conduct supervision and consumer protection.
fair_treatment_of_customers: Fair Treatment of Customers (FTC) is the fair market conduct principle that SBP emphasises alongside prudential regulation. Dedicated responsibility for conduct supervision under FTC has been assigned to the Consumer Protection Department.
consumer_education_material: SBP publishes consumer education material including: Rights and Responsibilities of Credit Bureaus' Consumers (Urdu); Protecting your Payment Cards; What are Bank Accounts?; How to use ATM/Debit Cards?; How to use Credit Cards?; How to protect yourself from Identity Theft?; Collection of Utility Bills by Banks; Fair Debt Collection Guidelines; Opening of Basic Banking Account; Priority to Senior Citizens and Visually Impaired People in Banking Services and Pension Disbursement Through Banks; Instructions on Service Charges; Statement of Account; Banking Services for the Visually Impaired Persons; Pension Disbursement Through Banks; Operational Guidelines on ATMs; and a Banking Glossary.
ecib_about: The Electronic Credit Information Bureau (eCIB) was established by the State Bank of Pakistan in December 1992 under Section 25(A) of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962. It gathers, organizes and disseminates data on borrowers' creditworthiness to help banks make informed decisions and to promote financial discipline across the industry.
ecib_legal_basis: The scope and activities of eCIB are governed under the provisions of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962. Section 25(A) vests powers with SBP to call for credit information in such manner as it may deem necessary and to make such information available to any banking company which is a member.
ecib_electronic_platform: The eCIB has evolved from a manual data system into a technology-driven platform. Introduced in April 2003, it allowed banks and financial institutions to directly upload and retrieve borrower data online, making Pakistan the first country in the region to offer such a facility.
ecib_coverage_and_members: eCIB maintains over four million borrower records across nearly 100 member institutions, ensuring comprehensive, secure and reliable data access. Under Section 25(A) of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962, credit information is made available to any banking company which is a member.
ecib_features: eCIB features include separate consumer and corporate reporting, credit history tracking, data correction, encryption, and validation to ensure data integrity. Its expanded coverage supports inclusive credit growth, enables risk-based lending and strengthens financial stability.
private_bureaus_list: The State Bank of Pakistan has issued licences to two private credit bureaus under the Credit Bureau Act, 2015: Aequitas Information Services Limited (AISL) and Data Check Limited (DCL). Both have commenced their operations.
private_bureau_services: Private credit bureaus augment the existing public system by offering additional services such as credit scoring, portfolio monitoring, anti-fraud tools and marketing analytics, supporting lenders in making more informed, timely and responsible credit decisions.
consumer_credit_report_rights: Private credit bureaus enable consumers to gain access to their credit information reports, dispute inaccuracies, and engage more proactively with their credit profiles. Reference material includes the booklet on the Rights and Responsibilities of Credit Bureaus' Consumers.
credit_bureau_legal_framework: Private credit bureaus are licensed and regulated under the Credit Bureaus Act, 2015. Related references include the Credit Bureau Act 2015, the Licensing Criteria for setting up a Credit Bureau in Pakistan, and the Rights and Responsibilities of Credit Bureaus' Consumers.
aisl_contact: Aequitas Information Services Limited (AISL): Regus Suite #102, 1st Floor, Bahria Complex III, M.T. Khan Road, Lalazar, Karachi. Helpline: 0308 8273337. Email: info@tasdeeq.com. Website: www.tasdeeq.com.
datacheck_contact: Data-Check Limited: Mezzanine Floor, Bahria Complex III, M.T. Khan Road, Karachi. Helpline: 021 35642320-27. Email: info@datacheck.com.pk. Website: www.datacheck.com.pk.
pep_definition: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are individuals who are entrusted with prominent public functions either domestically or by a foreign country — for example Heads of State or of government, senior politicians, senior government, judicial or military officials, and senior executives of state owned corporations, departments or autonomous bodies.
pep_non_discrimination: PEPs are not presumed to be high risk individually and must be treated in a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory manner by financial institutions. Financial institutions shall not discriminate on the basis of trade, region, gender or specific occupation, including a customer's status as a PEP. Banks have been directed not to refuse or restrict services to PEPs, including parliamentarians, on the basis of their affiliation or status.
pep_focal_person: Yes. SBP and all banks have nominated focal persons to deal with PEP matters. Banks are required to designate focal persons responsible for handling, monitoring and tracking all PEP-related requests and complaints, and must prominently display the contact details of their PEP focal persons at branches and on their websites, along with SBP's focal person details.
pep_escalation: If a PEP is not satisfied with the outcome of the complaint, or the grievance is not resolved within 15 days after registration of the complaint with the bank's focal person, he or she may directly contact the focal person appointed by SBP.
pep_account_opening_sop: Yes. The State Bank of Pakistan has devised Standard Operating Procedures to facilitate PEPs and streamline the account opening process. SBP has also prescribed SOPs defining timelines, responsibilities and reporting requirements for processing PEP-related requests, including account opening.
pep_sbp_unit_and_monitoring: SBP maintains a dedicated PEP unit within the Consumer Protection Department to take up unresolved PEP-related complaints with banks for expeditious resolution. Banks are required to report data on facilities extended to or declined for PEPs through regulatory returns, enabling SBP to monitor practices and identify gaps, and must resolve PEP complaints within the timelines prescribed under the CGHM, with SBP monitoring compliance.
pep_parliamentary_requests: All requests from parliamentarians must be routed through the bank's designated focal person to ensure oversight and consistency in handling.
clarify_complaint_stage: I can help with that. Have you already lodged the complaint with your bank's Complaint Management Unit, and if so, how many days ago? This determines whether the next step is the bank, the Banking Mohtasib Pakistan, or SBP.
clarify_institution_type: To guide you correctly, please confirm whether your complaint is against a bank, a Microfinance Bank (MFB) or a DFI. Microfinance consumers do not fall within the Banking Mohtasib's jurisdiction and should approach SBP.
clarify_credit_query: Could you confirm what you need? I can explain the eCIB maintained by SBP, the licensed private credit bureaus and their contact details, or how consumers can access and dispute their credit information reports.
followup_more_detail: Certainly. Please tell me which part you would like expanded — the complaint procedure, the applicable timelines, the relevant forum, or the contact details.
bmp_escalation_timeline_2024_law: As of the November 2024 amendment to Section 82D(2) of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962, the bank must respond to your written complaint within 30 days. If it fails to respond, or you are unsatisfied with the reply, you may file a complaint with the Banking Mohtasib within a further 30 days (the Mohtasib may condone a delay if there were sufficient grounds). Note: SBP's own website currently still displays the older 45-day figure, which has not yet been updated to reflect this 2024 legal change. To be safe, wait for whichever period your bank or the Banking Mohtasib's office confirms applies to your case, and keep written proof of when you first complained.
bc_frf_framework_overview: In October 2025, SBP issued BPRD Circular No. 04 of 2025, introducing the Business Conduct and Fair Treatment of Consumers Regulatory Framework (BC&FRF). It consolidates earlier circulars into a single framework built around six pillars: Governance & Oversight, Disclosure & Transparency, Fair Treatment and Business Conduct, Data Protection & Privacy, Dispute Resolution Mechanism, and Awareness & Capacity Building. It applies immediately to banks and DFIs (the Governance & Oversight pillar takes effect from January 1, 2026), and to Electronic Money Institutions from January 1, 2026.
secp_jurisdiction_exclusion: SBP does not have regulatory jurisdiction over Investment Banks, Modaraba Companies, or Leasing Companies. Complaints about these entities should be directed to the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) instead.
unclaimed_deposits_overview: Under Section 31 of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962, an account is classified as an unclaimed deposit if there has been no transaction or statement acknowledgment for ten years. Banks must surrender such deposits to SBP annually, except accounts belonging to minors, the government, or accounts frozen under UNSC resolutions, which are exempt. To reclaim funds, the account holder or their legal heirs can apply through the bank branch with a valid CNIC; for deceased account holders, if the unclaimed amount is below PKR 100,000, banks can process the refund with an indemnity bond and death certificate instead of a full succession certificate. For amounts above PKR 100,000, a succession certificate is required. Before transferring an inactive account to SBP, the bank must first send you a written notice (by registered post, to your last known address) giving you a further period to respond before the transfer proceeds — banks that skip this step have not followed the law correctly. Separately, if a bank later discovers it had a valid lien or right of set-off against an account it already transferred, it can submit a claim to SBP for that lien within 30 days of the transfer, under Section 31(9) of the Banking Companies Ordinance.
bmp_cannot_decide: The Banking Mohtasib cannot: order a bank to grant a loan, advance, or finance; direct a bank to reduce or waive mark-up simply because you consider it excessive, unless there is a contractual or regulatory violation; review a bank's commercial or published policy just because you disagree with it; issue a stay order; decide matters pending before a court or another legal forum; or reopen a matter already decided by SBP or a court.
unauthorized_transaction_bank_liability: If you notice an unauthorized or fraudulent transaction on your account, banks and MFBs are strictly liable to compensate you for losses arising from fraud or unauthorized transactions conducted via mobile or digital banking channels, under SBP's regulatory framework. A bank cannot simply refuse your claim by pointing to an SMS alert it sent you. Banks are required to maintain complete, untampered logs of digital transaction alerts, which must be produced to settle such disputes.
digital_channel_outage_reporting_rules: Under SBP's Guidelines for Downtime of Digital Channels/Services, banks must notify customers of any planned maintenance at least 2 days in advance. If planned maintenance overruns its scheduled window by more than 2 hours, the bank must immediately report this to SBP's Payment Systems Policy and Oversight Department. For an unplanned outage (e.g. a system crash), any disruption lasting more than 30 minutes must be reported immediately to both SBP and affected customers, with an estimated time of restoration. (These specific figures are as stated in the source research; please confirm current thresholds directly with SBP or the relevant circular before relying on them for an official submission.)
emi_wallet_transaction_limits: Electronic Money Institution (EMI) wallets have tiered transaction limits. A basic (Level 1) wallet typically has a lower monthly load/cash-in limit, while a Level 2 wallet — which requires biometric verification — allows a higher monthly limit. If your transaction is being blocked for exceeding a limit, you will usually need to complete biometric verification with your EMI to upgrade your wallet tier. (These specific figures are as stated in the source research; please confirm current thresholds directly with SBP or the relevant circular before relying on them for an official submission.)
sunwai_portal_liaison_requirements: Banks and financial institutions are required to update the status of complaints on SBP's Sunwai portal accurately and on a regular, timely basis. Each institution must nominate a senior officer as a dedicated liaison point for SBP, and must notify SBP's Consumer Protection Department promptly if that officer changes. (These specific figures are as stated in the source research; please confirm current thresholds directly with SBP or the relevant circular before relying on them for an official submission.)
agricultural_loan_recovery_notice: Agricultural loans can be recovered as arrears of land revenue under Section 25B of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962, but the bank cannot go straight to recovery proceedings. It must first give you written notice, at least 15 days before initiating proceedings, offering the option to repay via installments — land revenue recovery can only proceed if you fail to meet those installments. (These specific figures are as stated in the source research; please confirm current thresholds directly with SBP or the relevant circular before relying on them for an official submission.)
emi_customer_funds_protection: Your e-money wallet balance is protected even if the EMI itself runs into financial trouble. SBP's regulations require EMIs to hold 100% of outstanding customer e-money balances in dedicated safeguarding/trust accounts with licensed commercial banks, separate from the EMI's own business funds. These funds cannot be used by the EMI for lending or claimed by its commercial creditors — they are reserved solely for paying back wallet holders.
bank_liquidation_depositor_priority: If a bank goes into liquidation, the official liquidator is required to make priority payments to depositors within 90 days, under Section 58(1) of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962. (These specific figures are as stated in the source research; please confirm current thresholds directly with SBP or the relevant circular before relying on them for an official submission.)
recent_regulatory_changes_overview: Several recent changes affect banking consumer protection in Pakistan: the Banking Companies (Amendment) Act, 2023 expanded certain provisions to cover microfinance banks; the Banking Companies (Amendment) Act, 2024 (Act XXIX of 2024) reduced the bank/BMP complaint response window from 45 to 30 days (Section 82D); and a 2026 Law Reform Commission report has proposed further amendments to formally extend the Banking Mohtasib's jurisdiction to microfinance institutions — this is a proposed reform, not yet law.
high_court_business_stay_order: Under Section 45(1) of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962, a High Court cannot grant an immediate stay order protecting a bank from creditor lawsuits unless the application is accompanied by a formal SBP report certifying that the bank will be able to pay its debts if the stay is granted. Any such stay is capped at a maximum cumulative period of six months.
appeal_to_sbp_governor: Separately from a review petition to the Banking Mohtasib or a representation to the President, any bank, bank official, or complainant aggrieved by a Banking Mohtasib order has the right under Section 82E(4) of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962 to appeal directly to the Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan. This appeal must be filed within 30 days of the Mohtasib's order, and the Governor is required to decide it within 60 days.
